    <section class="home-section" id="about" aria-labelledby="about-title">
      <h2 class="section__title" id="about-title">About</h2>
      <p>I am an Ezra Systems Postdoctoral Associate in Systems Engineering at Cornell University, where I work with Professor Fengqi You on AI for materials processing. I completed my Ph.D. at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2026 under the supervision of Professor Jingcheng Wang.</p>
      <p>I develop learning methods for physical systems whose predictions are used to make an operating decision. The recurring question is whether the approximation error of a learned model changes the decision that follows from it, so I score a model by the operating cost, regret, and constraint violation it produces, not by prediction error alone.</p>
    </section>

        <dl class="program-key">
          <dt>Signals and fields</dt>
          <dd>Urban water demand and network pressure, day-ahead electricity price, and the temperature and composition fields of a processing step.</dd>
          <dt>Learned dynamics</dt>
          <dd>A forecast distribution over the scheduling horizon, or a neural operator that maps process settings and boundary conditions to a field trajectory.</dd>
          <dt>Operating decision</dt>
          <dd>Pump and purchase schedules, feedback control actions, and process set-points, each computed under physical and operating limits.</dd>
        </dl>
        <figcaption class="program-caption">Measured signals and fields train a model of the dynamics. The model is then used inside an optimization or control problem, and the decision it produces is scored. The dashed return path carries that score back to the model, so regret and constraint violation, rather than prediction error, become the signal that trains and tests it.</figcaption>
      </figure>

      <ul class="directions">
        <li class="d-forecast"><strong>Decision-focused forecasting under uncertainty.</strong> A probabilistic forecast is trained through the schedule it induces, so a forecast error is priced in operating cost instead of likelihood.</li>
        <li class="d-operator"><strong>Neural operators for distributed dynamics.</strong> An operator maps initial conditions, geometry, and forcing to a field trajectory. I test it on field error, rollout error, and the sensitivities that a controller or an optimizer actually reads.</li>
        <li class="d-control"><strong>Learning-based control.</strong> Model error accumulates over a control horizon. I study how much of it reaches the selected action, the closed-loop cost, and the constraint violation.</li>
        <li class="d-material"><strong>AI for materials processing.</strong> With Professor Fengqi You, I build operators that map process conditions and boundary inputs to evolving material state fields, then use their rollouts and sensitivities for process control and constrained optimization.</li>
      </ul>

          <h3 class="note__title"><a href="/thinking/#emergence-and-physical-intelligence">Emergence and physical intelligence</a></h3>
          <p>I do not expect physical intelligence to show the emergence reported for large language models. If a mechanism for wide transfer exists, it should come from structure rather than from parameter count, because the laws that govern a physical system have always turned out to be short.</p>
        </article>
